Pick a Map

BO3 tells one long story — the Aether saga. Primis (Richtofen, Dempsey, Takeo and Nikolai) chase the Summoning Key across dimensions, collecting the souls of their original selves one map at a time. Play in release order and the ending of one map is the opening of the next. Difficulty is about the main quest, not survival.

Before You Drop In

The stuff that works on every map — learn it once, use it six times.

New to BO3 Zombies? There is no Directed Mode in BO3 — quests are hidden easter eggs with no on-screen objectives, which is exactly what this guide is for. Learn the ropes on The Giant (no quest pressure, simple layout), then take on Der Eisendrache as your first full main quest.

Systems
Shared Systems — Every Map

How BO3 Zombies Works

Everything on this page works the same on all six maps. Learn it once here, then each map guide only has to teach you what's different. BO3 is the game that invented GobbleGums — and it plays by older, harder rules than BO6: no armor, no exfil, no Directed Mode.

The Rules Of BO3

RuleHow it worksWhat it means for you
One modeStandard round-based survival. Main quests are hidden easter eggs — no objectives on screen, ever.This guide (or a video) open beside you is the objective list. Learn quests step by step.
No armor, no exfilYour health is perks and positioning only, and a run ends when you go down or finish the quest. There is no extraction.Juggernog is life. A "successful" run is a quest clear or a personal-best round.
4-perk limitYou can hold four perks at once. GobbleGums (Perkaholic, On The House) and quest rewards are the only ways past the limit.Buy in priority order — your four slots are precious.
Specialist weaponsMost maps have a buildable specialist (sword, Ragnarok, Gauntlet…) that charges from kills and sits on its own button.It's a free panic button and often a quest tool. Charge it, don't sit on it.

Points, The Box & Pack-a-Punch

  • Points are everything: hits, kills, headshots and rebuilding barriers. Knife kills (130) and headshots pay best early — spend round 1–3 points on doors, not the Box.
  • The Mystery Box costs 950 a spin and moves after enough uses (watch for the Fire Sale). Wonder weapons are Box-or-build on most maps — each map guide says which.
  • Pack-a-Punch costs 5,000 and massively raises damage, magazine size and ammo, with a camo and random attachments. In BO3 you can re-pack for 2,500 to re-roll the attachments and camo — no other Zombies game does this.
  • Der Wunderfizz (on The Giant, Der Eisendrache and Zetsubou) sells a random perk for 1,500 — the cheap way to fill your four slots once the map's own machines are bought.
  • Liquid Divinium is the meta currency: earned from playing (roughly every few rounds, and from opening doors/using machines), spent in Dr. Monty's Factory — 1 Divinium for 3 random GobbleGums, 3 for a guaranteed Mega-or-better set.
Spending order that wins runs: doors toward power → Juggernog → Pack-a-Punch → Speed Cola / Double Tap → your map's wonder weapon → fill perks from machines or Der Wunderfizz → re-pack only when the points are spare.

All 9 Perk-a-Colas — Prices & Priority

Fixed prices (BO3 perks don't escalate like BO6's), four slots. Which machines exist changes per map — Der Wunderfizz fills the gaps. Buy in this order unless a quest step needs a specific perk first.

PerkPriceEffect & verdict
Juggernog2,500Roughly doubles your health. Buy first, every run, every map. Without it, two hits end you.
Quick Revive500 solo / 1,500 co-opSolo: revives you once per purchase (up to 3 per match) — a literal extra life. Co-op: revive teammates twice as fast.
Speed Cola3,000Reloads and barrier rebuilds twice as fast. The DPS perk — mandatory on boss fights and high rounds.
Double Tap Root Beer 2.02,000Every shot fires two bullets for the price of one — effectively double damage. Best value perk in the game after Jug.
Stamin-Up2,000Faster sprint and longer sprint. Training, boss arenas and big maps (Gorod, Zetsubou) run on it.
Widow's Wine4,000Getting hit can web zombies in place, and your grenades become web grenades. Expensive, superb crowd control. Shadows of Evil & Der Eisendrache (and Revelations via Wunderfizz luck).
Mule Kick4,000Carry a third weapon. Great for quest loadouts (build weapon + DPS + wonder weapon) — but you lose the third gun when you go down.
Electric Cherry2,000Reloading emits an electric shock that stuns nearby zombies, stronger the emptier the mag. Der Eisendrache & Zetsubou staple.
Deadshot Daiquiri1,500ADS snaps to the head and tightens hip-fire spread. The camo-grind perk — The Giant's specialty.

GobbleGums — BO3 Invented Them

Build a pack of five GobbleGums in the pre-game menu. In a match, the GobbleGum machine gives you a random gum from your pack — your first gum each round is free; extra activations in the same round cost rising points. You can hold up to three at once. Gums come from Dr. Monty's Factory, paid for with Liquid Divinium. Four rarities:

  • Ultra-Rare Mega — the game-breakers. Perkaholic (every perk on the map, instantly, ignoring the 4-perk limit), Round Robbin' (ends the round on the spot), Killing Time (freezes everything for 20 seconds), Shopping Free is Rare Mega — see below.
  • Rare Mega — Shopping Free (everything free for a minute — doors, perks, Box, Pack-a-Punch), Alchemical Antithesis (points convert to ammo for your current weapon), On The House (spawns a free random perk drop).
  • Mega — In Plain Sight (zombies ignore you for 10 seconds — the quest-step gum), Sword Flay, Anywhere But Here! is Classic but quest-critical on Zetsubou, Cache Back (spawns a Max Ammo) is Classic too.
  • Classic — free in the Factory, no Divinium needed: Anywhere But Here! (random teleport — required for a Zetsubou cog), Stock Option (shoot straight from your reserve ammo — no reloads), Always Done Swiftly, Arms Grace (keep your weapons when revived).

Quest Pack

Perkaholic · Anywhere But Here! · In Plain Sight · Alchemical Antithesis · Cache Back

Free perks, an emergency teleport (mandatory on Zetsubou), invisibility for fiddly steps, and ammo insurance.

Boss Fight Pack

Perkaholic · Killing Time · In Plain Sight · Shopping Free · Cache Back

Freeze the arena, vanish to revive or reposition, and never walk into a boss under-perked again.

High Round Pack

Perkaholic · Alchemical Antithesis · Stock Option · Round Robbin' · Cache Back

Ammo economy for round 40+: turn points into bullets, skip the reload, and bail out of a bad round entirely.

Enemies — And How To Drop Them

EnemyWhereCounter
Zombie / HellhoundEverywhereHeadshots and training (running the horde in a loop). Hellhound rounds are free Max Ammo rounds — finish with the knife early, a shotgun late.
MargwaShadows of Evil, RevelationsShoot the glowing mouths — only open mouths take real damage. Three heads, three kills' worth of patience. Li'l Arnies distract it.
ParasiteShadows of EvilSmall flying pests that spit. One clean shot each — clear them before they swarm a ritual or a train ride.
Insanity ElementalShadows of EvilFloating orbs that dive-bomb you. Shoot them at range; they're the flag-defense step's main threat.
KeeperShadows of Evil, Der Eisendrache, RevelationsFloating robed casters. Burst them down fast — in quests they're usually helping you, so read the step before you shoot.
PanzersoldatDer Eisendrache, RevelationsArmored mech suit with a flamethrower and claw. Shoot the head and the power core; upgraded bows melt it. Drops a Ragnarok part on Der Eisendrache.
ThrasherZetsubou No ShimaPlant-mutated brute that grabs and slams. Shoot the glowing spore on its body to enrage then kill it — or feed it to the Masamune.
SpiderZetsubou No ShimaWebs your screen and your movement. Spider rounds are a breather — melee and shotguns; save one for the KT-4 cage.
Valkyrie DroneGorod KroviFlying robot that shocks and marks you for the dragon. Shoot it down fast — and kill one next to the hatchery generator on purpose (quest step).
Mangler (Gorod)Gorod KroviSoviet armored soldier with a cannon arm. Shoot the arm to make it charge — you'll do it on purpose for S.O.P.H.I.A.'s escort task.
DragonGorod KroviNot killable in the open — it strafes areas with fire on a timer. Watch the sky, use its nests, and save the real fight for the boss arena.
Fury & Hellfire MargwasRevelationsElemental Margwa variants in the boss path. Same rule as Margwas: mouths, patience, distance.

Power-ups

  • Max Ammo, Insta-Kill, Double Points, Nuke, Carpenter, Fire Sale, Death Machine — dropped by zombies on every map. Save a Max Ammo grab for the end of a round when you can, and never waste an Insta-Kill on three zombies.
  • Free power-up hunts: several maps hide bonus drops behind small secrets — each map guide's Side section lists its map's set.
  • No exfil: BO3 predates it. Your run ends at the quest cutscene or on the floor — plan GobbleGums and Quick Revive accordingly.

Shadows of Evil
Launch Map · Morg City, 1940s

Shadows of Evil

Four sinners — Nero the magician, Jessica the femme fatale, Floyd the boxer, Vincent the crooked cop — wake up in a Morg City that the Shadowman has already fed to the Apothicons. Main quest: “Apocalypse Averted.” The honest warning first: the full quest requires four players — the final steps cannot be completed solo, though everything up to trapping the Shadowman can.

Numbered pins are the main quest in the order you run it; the Rift (and Pack-a-Punch) lies beneath the Junction, reached by the district portals. Lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “Apocalypse Averted” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “Apocalypse Averted”

The spine of the quest: four rituals open the Rift, every player builds and upgrades a sword, then the squad defends a flag in all four districts, traps the Shadowman, and stops the Giant Gateworm with the train. Beast Mode (activate at the purple-flamed braziers) is how you open half of this map — grapple, zap panels, and smash crates, all on a timer.

  1. Take the Summoning Key. In the spawn alley (Easy Street, Junction), use Beast Mode to smash the glowing crate in the back of the truck and pick up the Summoning Key. Nothing in this quest starts without it.
  2. Nero's ritual — Footlight District. Beast-grapple up to Nero's Landing and take the Lawyer's (Golden Fountain) Pen. Place it on the ritual table in Nero's ritual room, survive the ritual (Keepers attack; a Margwa may crash it), and pick up the Gateworm.
  3. Jessica's ritual — Canal District. Zap the panel to reach the Ruby Rabbit and take the Producer's Toupee. Run the ritual at the Ruby Rabbit altar, survive it, and take the Gateworm.
  4. Floyd's ritual — Waterfront District. Beast your way into the boxing gym, take the Promoter's Championship Belt, complete the gym ritual, and take the Gateworm.
  5. Vincent's ritual — Junction. Open the detective's office route near the Junction and take the Detective's Badge. Complete the fourth ritual and take the last Gateworm.
  6. Enter the Rift, unlock Pack-a-Punch. With four Gateworms, drop through a district portal into the Rift (the subway below the Junction). Place the worms on the four pedestals and the Summoning Key on the altar — after the countdown, Pack-a-Punch is open and the giant Apothicon appears in the sky.
  7. Build the Apothicon Sword (every player). Ride the train and memorize the three red symbols on the walls between districts. In Beast Mode at the underground station, zap those symbols into the wall to open it and take the egg. Place the egg on the Cthulhu statues (smash the chained boxes in Beast Mode to reveal them — one per district plus the subway) and kill the Margwa that spawns at each until the egg is charged. Return it to the wall and claim your sword.
  8. Upgrade to the Keeper Sword (every player). At your own character's ritual site, take the Arch-Ovum from the Keeper above the ritual table. Place it in the Rift's red circle and kill the Margwa that spawns there; repeat at the glowing circles until your sword is reborn as the Keeper Sword.
  9. Defend the flag — all four districts. Pick up the flag at the train junction, carry it to a district, plant it on the glowing purple spot and defend it from Insanity Elementals and the Shadowman (shoot him until he teleports away). Repeat in every district — each success pays a Max Ammo.
  10. Trap the Shadowman. All four players enter the Pack-a-Punch room and interact with the four Keepers to strip the Shadowman's shield. Shoot him as he teleports around the room; when he passes over the ritual table, interact with it instantly to pull him into the Summoning Key. Repeat until he's caught.
  11. Stop the Giant Gateworm. Three players become the Beast at the three train stations and electrify the Keepers/track switches while the fourth rides the train. Time the zaps as the train passes — hit the Gateworm with the train to finish the quest and roll the cutscene.

Wonder Weapons — Apothicon Servant & The Swords

The Apothicon Servant is built, not boxed — it fires a black-hole orb that vacuums up whole trains of zombies, and it's the best Margwa crowd-control on the map. Three parts, all drops:

  1. Margwa Heart: guaranteed drop from the first Margwa you kill — don't leave it on the floor.
  2. Margwa Tentacle: dropped by later Margwa kills (less common — keep killing them, especially during rituals).
  3. Xenomatter: dropped by Parasites and Insanity Elementals — farm the flying rounds.
  4. Assemble at a build bench (the Rift bench is the safest). The swords from quest steps 7–8 are your specialist slot: the Keeper Sword's dash and slam carry the flag defense.

Boss — The Shadowman & The Gateworm

  • The Shadowman can't be shot through his shield. In the Pack-a-Punch room, the four Keepers strip it — that's why this step is four-player only. Burn him fast each time the shield drops; slow damage lets him reset.
  • Bring: Pack-a-Punched automatic weapons (the Servant is for adds, not for him), Li'l Arnies to keep the room clear, and In Plain Sight gums for a safe revive or table interact.
  • The Gateworm finale is a timing step, not a damage step. The three Beast players zap their Keepers as the train approaches the worm; the rider calls the timing. Miss and you simply ride again — nobody dies for a failed pass.
  • Solo players: you can do everything through step 10's setup in a solo lobby, but the Keeper interact needs four hands — bring a squad for the clear and the "Apocalypse Averted" credit.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Civil Protector: find the three fuses (in Beast-zappable switch boxes across the Waterfront, Canal and Footlight districts), install them at the Junction fuse box, and spend points to summon a robot ally that fights and revives players.
  • Rocket Shield: three parts scattered through the districts — build it at a bench; the shield blast clears a path and it's near-mandatory for high rounds.
  • Widow's Wine hides in the Footlight theater — Beast-grapple to the balcony to reach the machine.
  • Train symbols & statues: the sword egg's three symbols change every game — write yours down on the first train ride instead of guessing later.
  • Der Wunderfizz sits in the Rift near Pack-a-Punch — the reliable way to finish a four-perk setup on this map.

Sources: Shadows of Evil — Nazi Zombies Wiki · Shadows of Evil main quest — Dexora

The Giant
Bonus Map · Der Riese Facility, 1945

The Giant

Der Riese — the Group 935 facility where Zombies began — remade as BO3's bonus map. There is no main quest here: the "route" below is the setup every good run follows — power, three teleporters, Pack-a-Punch, the Fly Trap secret — and then it's you, the catwalk, and the horde for as long as you last.

MapThe Run RouteWonder WeaponsHigh RoundsSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Run Route

The official Der Riese blueprint from the game's own artwork: Teleporter B at the top (Furnace Room), Teleporter C on the left, Teleporter A bottom right (the Lab), and the Mainframe on the right where every link lands. Numbered pins are the run route in order; lettered pins are side secrets. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the setup route in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

The Run Route — Setup, In Order

Seven steps and The Giant is fully open. Do them by round 7–9 and the rest of the run is perks, Pack-a-Punch and nerve.

  1. Spawn courtyard — bank points. You start in the main courtyard facing the Mainframe. Knife and headshot your way through the first rounds; open toward the power switch first, not the Box.
  2. Turn on the power. The switch is on the upper floor by the Generators, reached through the furnace-side building. Power wakes the perk machines, the teleporters and the traps.
  3. Link Teleporter B. Stand on the pad in the Furnace Room area (top of the blueprint), activate it, and sprint back to the Mainframe to complete the link before the timer runs out.
  4. Link Teleporter C. Same drill from the left-side pad by Animal Testing. Watch the courtyard windows on the run back.
  5. Link Teleporter A. The Lab pad, bottom right. All three linked is what wakes Pack-a-Punch — and each link can drop a Max Ammo on the Mainframe.
  6. Pack-a-Punch opens. The machine rises at the Mainframe. 5,000 for your main gun; save the 2,500 re-pack for when you're rich and picky about attachments.
  7. The Fly Trap. With a Pack-a-Punched weapon, shoot the Fly Trap control panel outside the fence by Teleporter B. Three hidden items appear around the facility (a teddy bear, a Monkey Bomb, a Juggernog bottle among the hiding spots) — shoot each one before it vanishes. Finish the set and the Annihilator specialist pistol waits in the Fly Trap furnace.

Wonder Weapons — Box Luck & The Annihilator

  • Wunderwaffe DG-2: Box-only on The Giant. Chain lightning that still deletes trains — the high-round dream roll, especially Pack-a-Punched.
  • Ray Gun: also in the Box. Reliable, splash-dangerous — pair it with careful positioning, there's no PhD Flopper in BO3.
  • Annihilator: earned, not rolled — complete the Fly Trap (route step 7). A one-shot-kill revolver on the specialist slot that recharges with kills; your get-out-of-a-corner card.
  • Monkey Bombs: in the Box and worth more than a wonder weapon on round 30 — a thrown Monkey is a free revive window.

High Rounds — The Catwalk Game

  • The Catwalk above the Animal Testing courtyard is the classic holdout: one direction of attack, a drop-off escape, and the whole map's spawns funnelling to you. It's why The Giant is BO3's camo and XP farm.
  • Loadout: Juggernog, Speed Cola, Double Tap, Deadshot (or Stamin-Up), a Pack-a-Punched wall gun you can re-ammo, and the DG-2 or a launcher for emergencies.
  • Traps are your economy: the electric traps by the teleporters chew through mid rounds for flat points — let them work while you hold the catwalk.
  • Hellhound rounds on The Giant are a breather and a Max Ammo — finish the last dog slowly and reload everything before it drops.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Der Wunderfizz stands in the Hangar/Garage area — 1,500 a spin for any perk on the map, the fastest route to a full setup.
  • The hidden song: shoot the three green flasks hidden around the facility to trigger the map's music easter egg.
  • Fly Trap leftovers: the trap's hidden items (teddy, monkey, bottle) are worth shooting even after the Annihilator — the set can be repeated for points and drops.
  • Radios & lore: the facility is full of Group 935 radios and the original Der Riese story beats — the furnace room and lab hold the best of them, including hints at what Primis did here.

Sources: The Giant — all secrets & easter eggs (Steam guide)

Der Eisendrache
DLC 1 · Griffin Castle, Austria

Der Eisendrache

Primis storms a Group 935 castle to erase the original Dempsey — and the castle answers with dragons, a Death Ray, and a moon that needs destroying. Main quest: “My Brother's Keeper.” The friendliest full quest in BO3 and the one to learn first: solo needs one upgraded bow, a full squad needs all four.

The overhead layout of Griffin Castle and its grounds: the castle cluster at lower right (courtyards, church and the Undercroft beneath), the rocket test site upper right, the tram station upper center, and the outer grounds to the left. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “My Brother's Keeper” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “My Brother's Keeper”

Nine stages. Everything hangs off the bow: feed the dragons, take the Wrath of the Ancients, upgrade at least one bow (all four in co-op ranked), then work the teleporter, the Death Ray and the Keeper.

  1. Feed the three dragons. Kill zombies in front of each dragon head until it eats its fill and flies off: above the Mystery Box in the Upper Courtyard (by Double Tap), above the fireplace in the Church, and beside the pyramid (MPD) in the Undercroft. Eight kills each, roughly.
  2. Take the Wrath of the Ancients. With all three dragons fed, claim the bow from the knight's tomb in the Undercroft. Then upgrade — the four elemental routes are in the Bows section below. Every player needs an upgraded bow before the wisp step works.
  3. Shoot the wisps. Fire the plain bow at the teleporter in the Undercroft until its prongs glow gold. A glowing wisp now hides on a random object somewhere in the castle — shoot it with an upgraded bow, then find the next. Four wisp hits charge the teleporter.
  4. Travel back in time. Everyone stands on the teleporter together. In the past (Dr. Groph's lab), grab the fuse and the glowing items, note the safe code from the clock/documents, and open the safe for the Tesla coils (rods) and the floppy disk before you're pulled back.
  5. Run the Death Ray. Install the fuse, set the Death Ray to Protect and fire it once. Then place the two rods, switch it to Destroy, and complete the Simon Says memory game on both computers (clock tower, then rocket test site). Press the green button — a rocket crashes into the courtyard. Take the golden Vril Device from the wreck.
  6. Escort the Keeper. Do the wisp hunt once more, travel back in time, and use the floppy disk to free the stone tablet. Place the Vril Device in the knight's tomb: a Keeper rises and walks the castle. At each of its four stops it draws a circle — get kills inside it with the bow the screen-tint names (light blue Wolf, dark blue Lightning, purple Void, red Fire). Finish by placing the tablet in the wall near Double Tap.
  7. Build the Ragnarok DG-4 (every player). Three parts: one drops from the first Panzersoldat you kill, one comes from riding a Wundersphere after the Death Ray sequence, and one from surviving the rocket test sequence at the test site. Build at a bench — you cannot enter the boss without them.
  8. Kill the Corrupted Keeper. Everyone places their Ragnarok on the glowing squares around the MPD in the Undercroft — you're pulled into the boss arena. Full fight guide below.
  9. Take Dempsey's soul. Back in the Undercroft, take the Summoning Key from the front of the MPD and place it on the computer by the clock tower. The rockets launch, Griffin Station dies, and the cutscene rolls.

The Four Elemental Bows

Each upgrade starts by claiming that bow's special arrow, then a short ritual chain, then charging the arrow in its elemental box beside the MPD. One bow per player — in a squad, split them up.

BowUpgrade route (short version)What it does
Kreeholo Lu Ahminhahr — Fire (Demon Gate)Shoot the glowing spots (clock tower wall, rocket-site rock, weather vane) to reveal the arrow; ride Wunderspheres through the three mid-air fire circles and fill each with kills; shoot the church fireplace with the symbol from the clock tower and follow the burning rocks to the arrow; charge it in the fire box.Magma eruptions that keep burning. The crowd-melter.
Kreeaho'ahm Nal Ahmhogaroc — Lightning (Storm)Wall-run across the five wind symbols in the Undercroft to start; charge the three urns (courtyard, church, rocket pad) with kills, then shoot their sparks into the three wood piles to light them; claim and charge the arrow in the lightning box.Chain-lightning storms. The Panzer and boss-add answer.
Wolf — HowlTake the arrow by the Death Ray; shoot the four wolf paintings around the castle in order; follow the ghost wolf and dig where it stops (three dig sites); charge the arrow with kills on the wolf platform by the rocket pad; forge it at the wolf box.Spirit wolves that maul whole trains. The easiest upgrade — do this one first.
Void — Skull CrusherShoot the purple symbol by Double Tap to start; kill a zombie on the glowing tile to free the urn; collect the six skulls hidden around the castle; feed Keeper crawlers to the skulls in the void room; charge the arrow in the void box.Black-hole skulls that drag zombies in. The trickiest upgrade, the strongest control.
Solo shortcut: in a solo game you only need one upgraded bow for the whole quest — Wolf is fastest, Lightning is strongest. In public/ranked co-op, every player needs their own upgraded bow.

Boss Fight — The Corrupted Keeper

  • The trap is the fight. The Keeper circles the arena throwing shockwaves and summoning skeletons and Panzersoldats. When the center of the arena glows, it moves to the middle — that's your window.
  • Slam the Ragnarok beneath it. A player plants the gravity spikes under the boss to pin it; its chest opens. Everyone fires uncharged bow shots into the chest core — charged shots waste the window.
  • Too slow = hide. If the chest closes, get behind a pillar before the lightning blast. Repeat the trap-and-burn cycle — three solid phases ends it.
  • Bring: upgraded bows (Lightning MVP), Jug + Speed Cola + Double Tap, and a Pack-a-Punched backup for skeletons. The arena has no ammo economy — spend everything.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Samantha's song: three radios hidden around the castle and grounds (marked on the map image itself) each play a lore transmission — find all three sets of speakers for the full story dump.
  • Rocket Shield: three parts (one rides the gondola route) — build it; the shield's blast is a real panic button on the rocket pad.
  • Wunderspheres (the low-gravity launch pads) aren't just transport — several bow steps and a Ragnarok part ride them, and the wall-runs between them hide ciphers.
  • Panzersoldat management: the first Panzer is a quest part — after that, they arrive on a timer. Upgraded bows and the Death Ray's Protect mode are the clean answers.

Sources: Der Eisendrache main quest — Dexora

Zetsubou No Shima
DLC 2 · Division 9 Island, Pacific

Zetsubou No Shima

An island where Division 9 grew weapons out of Element 115 water — and the island grew teeth back. Main quest: “Seeds of Doubt.” This is BO3's build-everything quest: the Skull, the KT-4, its upgrade, a gas mask, an electrified shield — and one GobbleGum (Anywhere But Here!) that is genuinely required. Load it in your pack before you start.

The real Division 9 map board from in-game: spawn at the bottom (“You Are Here”), Lab A on the left, Lab B on the right, the Bunker across the top with the Docks behind it. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “Seeds of Doubt” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “Seeds of Doubt”

Unlike the other maps, Zetsubou's steps run in parallel — builds first, then three cogs in any order, then the elevator. The route below is the efficient order. Prereqs running underneath everything: power needs both lab generators (bucket of water + generator parts at Lab A and Lab B), and every player must finish all three of their Trials of the Ancients at the podium by spawn.

  1. Spawn — Trials & the bucket. Grab the bucket (your water carrier for the whole map) and start your Trials of the Ancients at the podium. Trial rewards (including a free perk path) pay for the whole run — finish all three per player before the endgame.
  2. Lab A — power & the cage. Fill the bucket, restore Lab A's generator, and lower the cage trap: lure a spider inside during a spider round, raise it, and harvest the spider venom — KT-4 part one.
  3. Lab B — power & the webs. Restore Lab B's generator the same way. Power opens the Bunker and the ziplines. Keep the KT-4 in mind here: the webs at the back of the labs only melt for it.
  4. Build the Skull of Nan Sapwe. Four skulls hide near four ritual pedestals (spawn, the propeller trap, the docks zipline, and by the KT-4 benches near Mule Kick). Match each skull to the pedestal showing its symbol, defend it through its ritual, then take the cleansed skulls below and survive the Keeper lockdown to claim the Skull itself. Full detail in the KT-4 & Skull section.
  5. The Bunker — Pack-a-Punch & the blueprint. PaP lives in the Bunker. Then, in the bunker's purple-water room, use the Skull's Mesmerize on the torn poster to reveal the hidden half of the plans — and Mesmerize the blank wall beside the elevator to open the cog room behind it.
  6. Upgrade the KT-4 to the Masamune. Three more ingredients (Trials done, a spider boss, rainbow water) — full route in the next section. Only one player can hold the Masamune, and the boss needs it.
  7. Cog 2 — shoot down the plane. Grow a plant with blue water, shooting it with the KT-4 once a round for three rounds, until it yields a flak shell. Load the shell into the AA gun on the anti-aircraft platform and shoot down the plane when it passes — the cog lands somewhere on the island; watch where it falls.
  8. Cogs 1 & 3 — the secret room & the zipline. Cog 1: use Anywhere But Here! to teleport into the sealed room above Lab A and grab it off the floor. Cog 3: electrify your Zombie Shield at the Trials podium, ride the zipline, and melee at the right moment (solo: zap the zipline panel first) to drop onto the bridge and take it. Install all three cogs in the room behind the elevator.
  9. Ride the elevator — boss. Everyone puts on a Gas Mask (build it — no mask, no survival) and rides down. The Masamune burns the vines; the Giant Thrasher waits in its cage. Fight guide below.

Wonder Weapons — KT-4, Masamune & The Skull

The KT-4 fires acid that melts zombies, webs and the island's secrets alike. Three parts, built at the bench by the labs:

  1. Spider Venom: cage a spider in Lab A (quest step 2), raise the cage, take the venom.
  2. The Plant: plant a seed in any planter, water it with blue water from the bucket, and harvest the grown plant.
  3. The Flak Shell: grow a plant the same way near the AA platform route — its pod holds the shell the KT-4 needs (the same trick later feeds the AA gun for Cog 2).
  4. Masamune — the blue vial: with every player's Trials complete, the upgrade path opens; the vial waits with the Ancients' reward.
  5. Masamune — the spider tooth: melt the webs at the back of Lab A with the KT-4, kill the giant spider in its cave, cross the bridge and take the tooth from its mouth.
  6. Masamune — the rainbow plant: when a meteor shows in the sewer pipes, the water runs rainbow. Fill the bucket, Mesmerize the underwater cave wall with the Skull, plant a seed there and water it with rainbow water for three rounds. Build the Masamune at the bench beside the KT-4 table.
The Skull of Nan Sapwe is the other wonder weapon — a specialist that Mesmerizes hidden things into view (walls, posters, the blueprint) and freezes zombies in place. Half of this quest is invisible until the Skull shows it to you.

Boss Fight — The Giant Thrasher

  • Gas masks on, everyone. The elevator shaft and arena are toxic — a player without a mask goes down on the ride. Build masks from Thrasher/spore drops before you descend.
  • The Masamune opens the fight: burn the three vines blocking the hall, enter the cage room, and shoot the glowing spore on the Giant Thrasher's arm to start it.
  • Shoot the spores, not the Thrasher. New weak-point spores open on its arms and body as the fight goes on — the Masamune pops them; everything else is crowd control. Adds spawn after each spore — clear them, reposition, repeat.
  • Keep moving. The arena is tight and the Thrasher's slam is a down. Four destroyed weak points ends the fight, pays a Perkaholic, and rolls the darkest cutscene in BO3.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • The plant system is a whole second game: seeds + four waters (blue, green, purple, rainbow) + KT-4 shots grow different plants — free perks, free power-ups, clone plants that copy a player, and the AA shell all come out of planters.
  • Gas Mask: three parts from spores and Thrashers — build it early; it also makes the bunker's spore clouds free loot runs.
  • Electrified Shield: build the Zombie Shield, then charge it at the Trials podium until it crackles — the zipline cog and several secrets need the shock.
  • Skull pedestals: the four ritual sites (spawn, propeller trap, docks zipline, KT-4 benches) are worth learning cold — the Skull quest and half the map's Intel live on that circuit.
  • Trials of the Ancients: three personal challenges per player at the spawn podium — headshot streaks, melee kills and more — paying out perks and quest progress. Start them round 1.

Sources: Seeds of Doubt — Call of Duty Wiki · Zetsubou No Shima main quest — Dexora

Gorod Krovi
DLC 3 · Stalingrad, USSR

Gorod Krovi

Stalingrad — the City of Blood — where Group 935's dragons nest in the ruins and the original Nikolai makes his last stand in a stolen mech. Main quest: “Love and War.” The quest is run by S.O.P.H.I.A., Dr. Maxis's AI: power her up, feed her a code cylinder, collect six trophies, and survive her five tasks. Bring a shield, a Bowie Knife, and patience for the valve step.

MapMain QuestWonder WeaponsBossSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

S.O.P.H.I.A.'s own map screen from Dragon Command: Belinski Square (spawn) at the bottom, Dept. Store above it, Infirmary and Armory in the middle, Tank Factory left, Supply Depot right, Dragon Command at the top. The Hatchery and Pack-a-Punch are reached by dragon from Dragon Command. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “Love and War” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “Love and War”

Ten stages, run through S.O.P.H.I.A. in Dragon Command — check in with her screen between steps. Underneath the quest, Pack-a-Punch unlocks by riding a dragon to the Hatchery and slotting the three Code Cylinders (blue, yellow, red) earned from the area lockdowns in the Department Store, Supply Depot and Dragon Command.

  1. Belinski Square — spawn. You start in the square under the dragons. Work the early rounds here, grab the Zombie Shield parts as you push north, and open toward Dragon Command first.
  2. Power & S.O.P.H.I.A. — Dragon Command. Throw the power switch in the Dragon Command control room. S.O.P.H.I.A. wakes up — press the green button in front of her; she runs everything from here.
  3. The generator & the six valves. In the Hatchery basement (ride the dragon from Dragon Command), kill a Valkyrie Drone right next to the generator to start it. That lights the valve puzzle: six valves (Dragon Command, Armory, Supply Depot, Infirmary, Tank Factory, Dept. Store) must route pressure from the green-lit valve to the one holding the Master Code Cylinder. Note the start and end valves, work out each valve's setting (a valve solver earns its keep here), and turn them all within the time limit.
  4. Tank Factory valve. One of the six — upper levels, by the metal stairs. (Pins 4–7 mark the valve run; the order you visit them doesn't matter, the settings do.)
  5. Infirmary valve. By the beds on the way down through the Infirmary. Grab the trophy in this building while you're here — see step 8.
  6. Supply Depot valve. Beside the Mystery Box spawn point in the Depot. The Depot's safe also hides a GKZ-45 Mk3 part (Wonder Weapons section).
  7. Armory & Dept. Store valves. The last two on the run: Armory by the bridge, Dept. Store under the stairs. When all six are right, collect the Master Code Cylinder from the final tube, slot it into S.O.P.H.I.A., and shoot the password letters to spell KRONOS.
  8. Collect the six trophies. Hidden all over the city, in any order: shoot one down from the mural opposite the power room, melee one off a ledge with the shield, win them from a Mangler, a Valkyrie, the sewers and the Hatchery. Place each on S.O.P.H.I.A.'s trophy screen.
  9. Survive S.O.P.H.I.A.'s five tasks. In random order (the 935 lockdown is always last): Bomb Defusal — note the flashing order on her screen, defuse six bombs in that order in about a minute; Mangler Escort — shoot a green-eyed Mangler's arm off and walk it onto the Dragon Command pad; Valkyrie Escort — carry the injured drone from behind the barriers to its pad, slowly; Gersch Device defense — protect the device while it charges; Server Lockdown — survive the Hatchery lockdown. Finish all five and S.O.P.H.I.A. hands over the power core.
  10. Send the dragon, then Nikolai. At spawn, use your Gauntlet's dragon to carry the power core to Nikolai's stalled mech. Return to Dragon Command, stand on the grate where S.O.P.H.I.A. stood, and descend to the boss arena. Fight guide below.

Wonder Weapons — Mk3, Dragon Strike & The Gauntlet

  • Dragon Strike: at the Hatchery console, every player interacts within seconds of each other to start a four-wave lockdown — survive all four (left, right, back, then everywhere) and take the Dragon Strike controller. It calls a dragon strafing run anywhere outdoors; the quest uses it constantly.
  • Gauntlet of Siegfried — the egg: shoot the dragon egg down from above the sewer entrance in the Hatchery basement and carry it to a dragon nest to warm it (a dragon's fire breath or a Dragon Strike does it).
  • Gauntlet challenges: check in at the graves in Belinski Square and complete the whelp's trials in order — kill zombies burning in dragon fire, score penetrating multi-kills, then melee kills — then incubate the egg in the Hatchery until it hatches. The Gauntlet is a flamethrower fist with a baby dragon riding it, and its dragon carries the quest's power core.
  • GKZ-45 Mk3: the dual-wield Ray Gun Mark III combo, built from three parts — one in the Supply Depot safe, one from the Tank Factory, one from the Infirmary side of the map. The left gun's mist slows zombies and speeds you up; firing the Ray Gun into the mist collapses it into a black hole. The boss-fight weapon.
  • Upgrade the Dragon Strike: use the controller on the marked nests and complete its short trial chain to strengthen the strafes — worth it before the bomb-defusal task and the boss.

Boss Fight — The Dragon, Then Nikolai

  • Part one: the dragon. In the arena beyond the square, Nikolai's dragon attacks first — shoot its glowing weak points as it strafes, and keep off the burning ground. Manglers and Valkyries join in; the GKZ-45 Mk3's black hole is your crowd answer.
  • Part two: Nikolai 1.0. The mech powers up: machine guns, an electric harpoon, and missile salvos. Shoot the yellow lights/cores on the mech as they expose; when a core pops, the mech staggers — pour everything in.
  • Survival rules: never stand in the open during a salvo (the arena's cover is there for this), keep a Dragon Strike in reserve for add waves, and let one player run the Gauntlet's dragon breath as a flamethrower wall.
  • The ending: when the mech dies, Nikolai's soul goes into the Summoning Key — the last of the four. The cutscene sets up Revelations directly.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Guard of Fafnir: the dragon shield — three parts around Dragon Command and the Dept. Store. Its fire blast counts for the Gauntlet's first challenge and its bash knocks a trophy loose.
  • “Ace of Spades” song: find the three ace of spades cards hidden around the city to play the map's Motörhead easter egg.
  • The Mangler helmet: complete the challenge podium tasks and a Mangler's helmet becomes wearable — protection and a trophy-path shortcut in one.
  • Dragon nests: the nests on the rooftops are fast-travel and egg-warming spots — and the safest place to watch a strafing run you called in yourself.

Sources: Gorod Krovi main quest — Dexora · Love and War — codzombies.app

Revelations
DLC 4 · The House & The Apothicon

Revelations

The Aether saga's finale. Maxis freed the Shadowman, the Apothicons ate the world, and what's left is a house surrounded by floating shards of every map you've ever played — Nacht der Untoten, Verrückt, Kino der Toten, Mob of the Dead, Shangri-La, Der Eisendrache and more, stitched together by jump pads and portals. Main quest: “For The Good Of All.” You'll need Li'l Arnies and the Apothicon Servant from the Box — start spinning early.

MapMain QuestWonder WeaponsBossSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

Revelations never shipped with an in-game tac-map — the overview below shows the floor plan of each classic area the world is stitched from, and each pin sits on the area its step happens in: The House (spawn) at the bottom, Nacht center, Kino top right, Mob of the Dead left, Der Eisendrache right. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “For The Good Of All” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “For The Good Of All”

Nine stages. The quest is a tour of Zombies history: shoot the graves, build a Keeper, play three film reels, aim four engines at Nacht, raise four Gateworms, and throw the Summoning Key at seven pieces of history before facing the Shadowman one last time.

  1. Shoot the graves. Left of the spawn room at The House, four gravestones bear the heroes' names. Shoot them in this order: Richtofen, Dempsey, Takeo, Nikolai. The quest is awake.
  2. Override the four Corruption Engines. One engine per island (500 points each) — activate it and survive while it charges. All four online opens the portals to Nacht der Untoten and the path into the giant Apothicon, where Pack-a-Punch waits inside the beast.
  3. Build the Keeper Protector. Three parts across the islands — the flag (Origins/Mob side), the skull (Verrückt), the stone/crystal (Der Eisendrache/Kino side). Build it at any altar; for 5,000 points the Keeper fights beside you, revives you, and its ritual starts the reel hunt.
  4. Reel 1 — the Keeper ritual. Summon the Keeper Protector at the Nacht altar and complete its ritual to earn the first audio reel. Play reels at the projector in Kino der Toten as you earn them.
  5. Reel 2 — feed the Apothicon's holes. Inside the Apothicon (entered through its mouth in the Der Eisendrache area), throw Li'l Arnies into the holes in the walls — three holes per set, finish a set before leaving or it resets. The Servant's upgrade rocks are here too: shoot the five floating rocks to unlock its Pack-a-Punch upgrade.
  6. Reel 3 — Sophia's bones. With the upgraded Apothicon Servant, shoot the six bones hidden around the islands (spawn, Origins, Verrückt, Der Eisendrache, Shangri-La, Nacht), then the bones and Sophia's body upstairs in Nacht. Take the third reel, play it in Origins, and meet Sophia in her robot form back in Nacht.
  7. Aim the engines, fetch the Kronorium. At each Corruption Engine, use its turret (2,000) to shoot the blue crystal until the beam locks onto Nacht — all four aligned wakes Sophia fully. Escort her to Kino, ride the teleporter to Samantha's room in The House, take the Kronorium from the bed, and place it on the podium on the Kino stage.
  8. Eggs, runes & the Margwa arena. Collect an Apothicon egg, hatch Gateworms, and hunt the four Runes of Creation across the islands. With all four runes, stand on the projector rune in Kino to teleport into the arena: survive four elemental waves (anti-gravity, fire, lightning, void) against Margwas, then take the Summoning Key from the center. Now throw the Key at seven relics — the Kino chandelier, the Der Eisendrache clock, the Shangri-La focusing stone, the Origins tombstone, the Mob of the Dead poster, the Verrückt fountain, and the red barrel in Nacht.
  9. Face the Shadowman. Regroup, re-perk, and take the Kino teleporter into the final arena. Fight guide below — finishing it ends the match and the BO3 story.

Wonder Weapons — Servant, Keeper & Arnies

  • Apothicon Servant: Box-only here — the black-hole gun from Shadows of Evil, and the quest's skeleton key. Spin for it from round 1; the quest cannot finish without it.
  • Upgrade it: inside the Apothicon, shoot the five floating rocks while it's equipped to unlock the 5,000-point Pack-a-Punch upgrade — bigger holes, more ammo, and the bone-shooting the Sophia step needs.
  • Keeper Protector: built (quest step 3) and summoned for 5,000 at any altar — a friendly Keeper that kills, distracts and picks you up. The best solo insurance in BO3.
  • Li'l Arnies: Box tactical, and a quest item — the Apothicon's holes only accept Arnies. If the Box gives them to you early, resist wasting them on random rounds.

Boss Fight — The Shadowman, Last Time

  • Same rules as Morg City: the Shadowman is invulnerable inside his shield. Place the Summoning Key on one of the four glowing green altars and kill zombies around it — roughly ten souls charge it.
  • Throw the charged Key at Sophia. She hovers mid-arena; her beam strips his shield. Now shoot him with fast automatic weapons — black-hole weapons don't move him, bullets do.
  • Push him into the Apothicon's mouth. He teleports as he takes damage; herd him backward across the arena until he's inside the mouth behind the Kronorium — then interact with the book on the pedestal immediately.
  • Bring: Tier-packed automatics, the upgraded Servant for adds, full perks and a Keeper Protector watching your back. Winning ends the game on the spot — finish your side content first.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • The Zetsubou shard and the other mini-areas hide masks, hats and trial stones — the island-hopping secrets reward players who check every jump pad.
  • The audio reels (Nacht chair, Verrückt wheelchair, Mob box — and the three quest reels) play at the Kino projector: the whole Aether story, in order, in one room.
  • Shangri-La's focusing stone is one of the seven Key throws — and the area around it hides some of the map's best training ground for the arena waves.
  • Nacht, downstairs: where it all started in 2008 — the Keeper altar here, the help-room door, and the first window every Zombies player ever boarded. Take a second before the boss.

Sources: Revelations main quest — Dexora

Camos & Grind
Progression

Camos, Divinium & The Grind

The long-term chase in BO3: Dark Matter on your guns, a GobbleGum collection worth having, and Master Prestige. BO3's camo challenges can be progressed in Zombies — the horde is the fastest target range ever made.

The Road To Dark Matter

Every weapon climbs the same ladder. Check the exact counters on the weapon's challenge card — headshot and kill totals vary by weapon class, and Zombies kills count.

  1. Base camos (per weapon): work through the weapon's camo challenges — headshots first (the big counter), then the situational sets (rapid kills, longshots don't apply in Zombies; kills after reloading, without attachments, and so on).
  2. Gold: unlock every base camo for that weapon. Gold is per-weapon and purely a challenge grind — The Giant's catwalk with Deadshot Daiquiri is the classic farm.
  3. Diamond: earn Gold on every weapon in a class (all assault rifles, all SMGs…). Diamond unlocks per class, so finish classes, don't scatter.
  4. Dark Matter: earn Diamond on every class. The animated black-and-purple finish is BO3's ultimate flex — and in Zombies it can be earned entirely against the horde.
  5. Zombies-side chase: high-round calling cards, quest completion emblems, and the Super Easter Egg reward — complete the main quests on Shadows of Evil, Der Eisendrache, Zetsubou, Gorod Krovi and Revelations on one account to earn the Summoning Key gateworm calling card and a permanent head-start: every Revelations run begins with the RK5 upgraded path and bonus GobbleGum credit toward the next quest.
Fastest loop: The Giant, catwalk spot, Deadshot + Double Tap, train the courtyard spawns through the teleporter rooms. Headshots stack fast, dogs give free Max Ammos, and a failed run costs you nothing but time.

Liquid Divinium — Spend It Right

Divinium drips in just by playing — rounds survived, doors opened, machines used — and Dr. Monty's Factory turns it into GobbleGums. The math that matters:

  1. 1 Divinium = 3 random gums (any rarity). Fine early, when any Mega is an upgrade.
  2. 3 Divinium = a guaranteed Mega-or-better pull — the only sane way to hunt Perkaholic and the other Ultra-Rares once your Classics are stocked.
  3. Farm it where you farm everything: long games pay best. A 30-round Giant run or a full quest clear earns more Divinium than five short games — and the quest maps pay a completion bonus in gums and XP.
  4. Prestige: 55 levels, 10 prestiges, then Master Prestige climbing to level 1000. Prestiging resets your unlocks but not your camos, gums or quest completions — your Dark Matter progress is safe.
